overview.headline: Copying small DNA segments for lab study

keyPoints.point: This technique is used to amplify small segments of DNA to provide amounts needed for study.
keyPoints.quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a technique used to "amplify" small segments of DNA.

keyPoints.point: This method acts as molecular photocopying, a fast and inexpensive technique to copy small segments of DNA.
keyPoints.quote: the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a fast and inexpensive technique used to "amplify" - copy - small segments of DNA.

keyPoints.point: Copied DNA supports laboratory and clinical work including fingerprinting and detection of bacteria or viruses.
keyPoints.quote: including DNA fingerprinting, detection of bacteria or viruses (particularly AIDS), and diagnosis of genetic disorders.

keyPoints.point: This cycle of denaturing and synthesizing new DNA is repeated as many as 30 or 40 times to duplicate the original segment.
keyPoints.quote: The cycle of denaturing and synthesizing new DNA is repeated as many as 30 or 40 times

keyTerms.gloss: fast and inexpensive technique to copy small segments of DNA
keyTerms.quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a technique used to "amplify" small segments of DNA.

keyTerms.gloss: isolated pieces needing amplification for study
keyTerms.quote: studies of isolated pieces of DNA are nearly impossible without PCR amplification.

keyTerms.gloss: enzyme that builds new strands using original strands as templates
keyTerms.quote: Next, an enzyme called "Taq polymerase" synthesizes - builds - two new strands of DNA, using the original strands as templates.

keyTerms.gloss: heated separation into pieces for copying
keyTerms.quote: To amplify a segment of DNA using PCR, the sample is first heated so the DNA denatures, or separates into two pieces of single-stranded DNA.

keyTerms.gloss: machine programmed to alter temperature every few minutes
keyTerms.quote: directed by a machine called a thermocycler, which is programmed to alter the temperature of the reaction every few minutes
